title: Intake gate and dependency matrix for open-model release channels
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define a prescriptive intake gate, dependency matrix, and release-channel definitions for new community/open models entering the Redwood model catalog. The goal is to reduce runtime surprises (latency regressions, KV/cache incompatibilities, tokenization mismatches) and make pinning/upgrade decisions deterministic for product teams and runtime engineers.
background: Over the past 6 months we saw 4 incidents where unpinned community model variants caused latency regressions or incorrect outputs due to subtle runtime incompatibilities (quantization layout, KV cache format, or tokenizer differences). Current onboarding notes are free-form; eng teams must investigate model-by-model. We need a compact prescriptive intake checklist and a dependency matrix that maps model characteristics to required runtime/serving guardrails and a clear release-channel (edge/stable/experimental) classification.
proposal_summary: Introduce a 3-channel release model (experimental, edge, stable) and a dependency matrix that lists required compatibility signals. Each intake must produce: (1) an automated runtime compatibility report produced by the profiling harness, (2) a pinning recommendation (pin/unpin/managed-rollout), and (3) a fallback plan. Create an intake gate checklist that gates listing a model in the catalog's edge/stable channels. Define metrics-sentinels for automatic rollback (latency thresholds, tokenization failure rate, perplexity drift on internal evals).
scope_in_scope_out: IN SCOPE: define intake gate checklist and machine-readable compatibility matrix
IN SCOPE: define release channel semantics and pinning decision rules
IN SCOPE: acceptance criteria and rollout/rollback sentinels
OUT OF SCOPE: implementing UI in Console (separate ticket for Console UX)
OUT OF SCOPE: automatic quantization transformations (handled by runtime)
compatibility_matrix_requirements: tokenizer: BPE vs unigram vs sentencepiece + canonical vocab mapping (required)
kv-cache-format: layout identifier and supported flush/restore semantics
attention-type: causal vs prefix-tuning/decoder-only vs encoder-decoder
layer-file-format: expected model repo layout and parameter sharding descriptors
max_sequence: declared max_seq_len and observed OOM risk profile
quantization-compat: supported quantization bitwidths and hetereogeneous kernel availability
op-level-coverage: runtime coverage report (missing/custom ops flagged)
preferred-batch-behavior: batching compatibility notes and optimal request sizing
pinning_policy_summary: Stable channel: model variants must be pinned to a specific artifact digest/hash. Only security/patch releases allowed; semver minor bumps require regression tests.
Edge channel: allowed to have rolling artifacts; requires automated canary + perf guardrails with 24h burn-in and explicit rollback thresholds.
Experimental: unpinned by default for research use; must include explicit warning and rate-limiting to protect host infra. No SLA.
Pinning recommendation generation: intake tooling will produce one of {PIN_REQUIRED, PIN_RECOMMENDED, UNPIN_RECOMMENDED} with rationale.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable intake schema (JSON) exists that captures the compatibility matrix fields and can be produced by the profiling harness
A documented release-channel definition (experimental/edge/stable) with examples and allowed operations for each channel
A deterministic rule-set that maps compatibility signals to a pinning recommendation (PIN_REQUIRED/PIN_RECOMMENDED/UNPIN_RECOMMENDED) and is reviewed by runtime and infra leads

A list of 5 sentinel metrics and specific numeric thresholds for automatic rollback on edge/stable (e.g., +25% latency P95, >1% tokenization failure, >10% degraded quality on core eval prompts), with owners assigned for each metric
An intake checklist template and a minimal PRD template for catalog entries, including required links to: model weights, tokenizer tests, profiling artifacts, and license/compliance notice
A sample of 3 community models (one per channel) processed end-to-end through the intake, producing compatibility reports and pinning decisions documented in the ticket attachments
Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime Engineering (Diego Martinez), Security (Priya Nair), and Developer Experience (Harrison Liu)
rollout_plan: Week 1: finalize intake schema and dependency matrix; share with runtime and infra for feedback
Week 2: run profiling harness on 10 candidate community models and produce sample compatibility reports
Week 3: iterate thresholds with runtime on observed distributions; finalize sentinel numeric thresholds
Week 4: publish intake checklist + PRD template and pilot on 3 incoming model PRs to the catalog
Post-pilot: create follow-up tickets for Console integration and automation of recommendation generation
qa_checks: Verify profiling harness produces a parsable JSON report for every model in the pilot set
Run tokenization round-trip tests on canonical inputs and ensure <0.1% mismatch rate for edge/stable candidates
Confirm runtime can load and run the model on dedicated CI infra with expected memory/latency profile
Validate fallback routes (e.g., stable->edge->fallback-model) are configured for edge/stable entries and exercised in canary
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Strict pinning increases operational friction for community model updates. Mitigation: define a lightweight re-certification path for patch fixes and automate regression tests.
Risk: False negatives in the profiling harness may miss custom ops. Mitigation: require op-coverage report and manual review for edge/stable channel candidates.
Risk: Teams may game the channel classification. Mitigation: require runtime sign-off before moving to edge/stable and audit logs for channel changes.
Risk: Sentinels too conservative leading to frequent rollbacks. Mitigation: run sensitivity analysis across historical model runs to calibrate thresholds.
